current_focus.domain: cms-first-013 slice 1 (no gates): the CMS owns content and the repository owns structure; scripts/cms-mirror.mjs (export the CMS into seed/seed.json, open the cms-edit PR, --check); cms:sync slimmed to schema only; the Worker mirror on publish/unpublish and the failure email through a Cloudflare Email Routing send_email binding, both dormant until their bindings and secrets exist; the namespace gate's machine-identity rules (reads and _rev-bearing draft writes only); check:live redefined; the cms-edit auto-merge workflow; docs, AGENTS.md, proof
current_focus.summary: Maintainer 'go; use cloudflare email routing' on 2026-10-07 for slice 1 of cms-first-013 (no gates): (1) scripts/cms-mirror.mjs: reads the live CMS pages (identity ladder as the sync), writes them into seed/seed.json (pages only; block types and collections stay as the repo says and schema drift is reported), and unless --check or --no-pr pushes a cms-edit/<timestamp> branch from origin/main and opens a PR 'CMS edit: ...' labelled cms-edit; --check exits 1 when the repo differs from the CMS and names the fixing command. (2) scripts/cms-sync.mjs becomes schema-only (block types create/update/activate; never writes page content; EmDash setup is the one-time bootstrap). (3) A Worker module triggered by a successful POST .../publish or .../unpublish on pages: after the response (waitUntil) it reads the live pages from D1, builds the seed, and through a GitHub fine-grained token (secret GITHUB_MIRROR_TOKEN, repo from a var) creates a branch, commit and PR with the cms-edit label; it never merges; on any failure it emails agent@smokyproduct.co (recipient from a var, sender mirror@repoglance.com) through a send_email binding with the page, the error and the npm run cms:mirror re-run; when the token or the email binding is absent it logs that it is unconfigured and does nothing else (dormant until slice 2). (4) src/namespace-gate.ts admits a machine identity (an Access JWT with common_name and no email, verified with jose against the team's JWKS and audience, carrying an EmDash Bearer token) only to GET on content and schema routes, PUT on a content entry whose JSON body carries a non-empty _rev and no status other than draft, POST create with status draft, and POST .../preview-url; everything else answers 404; unit-tested. (5) scripts/live-check.mjs: a difference now means the repo is behind the CMS (run cms:mirror) and the live source is expected to be cms. (6) .github/workflows/cms-edit-automerge.yml arms auto-merge (merge commit) for cms-edit PRs on cms-edit/* branches with the repository token. (7) Docs: AGENTS.md boundaries (CMS owns content, repo owns structure, agents draft only, the mirror), docs/cms-access.md runbook, README, docs/content.md, docs/getting-started.md; wrangler.jsonc declares the send_email binding and the vars; prepare-deploy passes them through; jose pinned as a direct dependency. (8) Proof under proof/cms-first-20261007/PROOF.md and .grilltrack/proof/cms-first-013-verify-20261007.md: unit tests, npm run verify, a dev-server round trip (bootstrap, an admin-style publish, mirror --check and --no-pr showing the edit, the Worker trigger against a local GitHub stub), a separate read-only review on the exact commit, commit with the trailer, push, PR against main. Slice 2 (gates, maintainer): the GitHub token secret, repo auto-merge on, a ruleset on main requiring the site checks, Email Routing on repoglance.com with agent@smokyproduct.co verified and the send_email binding, deploy, one real edit and one forced failure. Slice 3 (gates, later): the agent draft lane. No merge, deploy, Cloudflare, DNS, Access or secret action by the agent.

decisions.question: How do seed/seed.json (copy, imagery slots, block types) and the EmDash CMS on repoglance.com stay equal, so the live site never silently diverges from the locked content again: which is the source, how does it reach the other, with which identity and trigger, and what proves the live site equals the seed?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer's answer 'D' to the four options presented with their gates and costs. Facts behind the shape: EmDash 1.0.1's client and CLI accept a cloudflared-cached Access JWT (cf-access-token), so the maintainer's own identity drives the API with no new Cloudflare resource; a service-token JWT carries no email and would need a Service Auth policy, a service token, an EmDash API token and a guard change (documented as the unattended option, not built); removing a select option is a breaking block-type change in EmDash 1.0.1, so the sync creates and activates a new version and migrates the blocks; the CMS must be written only after the Worker that renders the new seed is deployed, so the trigger is the deploy runbook, never the merge. Options A (seed only), B (sync without the live check) and C (CMS as source, seed exported) were not chosen. Builds on the closed track's site-copy-006, site-imagery-007 and cms-access-008 (.grilltrack/archive/gt-20261001102301-89ec89/).

decisions.choice: CMS-first (maintainer, 2026-10-07, with four amendments). (1) The CMS owns content: an edit published in the EmDash admin is live and persists; nothing ever writes copy from seed/seed.json into the CMS after the one-time bootstrap. (2) The repository owns structure: block types, components, image slugs, the Worker; they reach the CMS by deploy and a schema-only sync. (3) The site mirrors itself into the repository on publish and unpublish, with no schedule: after answering the admin's request the Worker builds the seed from the CMS, pushes a branch and opens a PR titled 'CMS edit: ...' labelled cms-edit through a GitHub fine-grained token scoped to this repository that may push a branch and open a PR and never merges; a repository workflow arms auto-merge for cms-edit PRs and branch protection lets them merge only when the checks are green; a published edit that fails a truth test leaves its PR open and red. (4) If the mirror fails for any reason (GitHub unreachable, token error, anything) the Worker sends a failure email to agent@smokyproduct.co naming the page, the error and how to re-run npm run cms:mirror; it never fails silently; npm run cms:mirror is the manual and on-touch safety net (every agent session and the schema sync start with it). (5) Agents only write drafts, never publish: a machine identity (Access service token plus a draft-scoped EmDash API token) is admitted by the namespace gate only to read and to write drafts; publish, unpublish, schedule, delete and schema writes answer 404 to it; the agent hands the maintainer EmDash's preview link and the admin link, and the maintainer edits and publishes in the admin. (6) Before writing a draft the agent reads the page's current revision and writes against it: the gate refuses a machine draft write that carries no _rev, and EmDash refuses one whose _rev is stale (409), so the agent re-reads and redoes the draft on the newer version. (7) A brand-new site's first CMS load comes from the seed through EmDash setup, once.

history.choice: CMS-first (maintainer, 2026-10-07, with four amendments). (1) The CMS owns content: an edit published in the EmDash admin is live and persists; nothing ever writes copy from seed/seed.json into the CMS after the one-time bootstrap. (2) The repository owns structure: block types, components, image slugs, the Worker; they reach the CMS by deploy and a schema-only sync. (3) The site mirrors itself into the repository on publish and unpublish, with no schedule: after answering the admin's request the Worker builds the seed from the CMS, pushes a branch and opens a PR titled 'CMS edit: ...' labelled cms-edit through a GitHub fine-grained token scoped to this repository that may push a branch and open a PR and never merges; a repository workflow arms auto-merge for cms-edit PRs and branch protection lets them merge only when the checks are green; a published edit that fails a truth test leaves its PR open and red. (4) If the mirror fails for any reason (GitHub unreachable, token error, anything) the Worker sends a failure email to agent@smokyproduct.co naming the page, the error and how to re-run npm run cms:mirror; it never fails silently; npm run cms:mirror is the manual and on-touch safety net (every agent session and the schema sync start with it). (5) Agents only write drafts, never publish: a machine identity (Access service token plus a draft-scoped EmDash API token) is admitted by the namespace gate only to read and to write drafts; publish, unpublish, schedule, delete and schema writes answer 404 to it; the agent hands the maintainer EmDash's preview link and the admin link, and the maintainer edits and publishes in the admin. (6) Before writing a draft the agent reads the page's current revision and writes against it: the gate refuses a machine draft write that carries no _rev, and EmDash refuses one whose _rev is stale (409), so the agent re-reads and redoes the draft on the newer version. (7) A brand-new site's first CMS load comes from the seed through EmDash setup, once.

decisions.question: Who owns the content of repoglance.com, who owns its structure, how does the repository learn about edits made in the EmDash admin, what may an agent do in the CMS, what happens when the mirror fails, and how is a fresh site bootstrapped?
decisions.rationale: Replaces cms-sync-011 (option D), reopened on the maintainer's instruction: an admin who logs in to make a change expects it to persist, and people letting agents build will want to log in and override. Alternatives weighed: E (admin wins, repo follows through an export PR, conflict-aware sync) kept two writers of content and a manual export; a scheduled mirror was rejected for a site edited months apart; agents editing the CMS directly without a human gate was rejected because the truth rules exist to stop unproven claims. EmDash 1.2 facts behind the shape: no outbound webhooks but host hooks on publish/unpublish and waitUntil in the Worker; roles have no edit-any-without-publish tier and tokens belong to the user who creates them, so the draft-only rule lives in our gate; PUT /content accepts _rev and answers 409 on a stale revision.

site-links-010 and the Play opt-in link: maintainer actions outside the repo (the Play listing's website field, the RepoGlance README pointing at repoglance.com, the opt-in link when Play Console shows it), each a seed change that reaches the live site through cms:sync and check:live.
recommendation.reason: The sync and the live check exist and are proven locally, but both run only when the maintainer runs them; the invariant the maintainer asked for ('never silently diverges') is strongest when the live check also runs on a schedule. The other candidates are hygiene or outside actions, not product decisions.
recommendation.recommended: live-check-schedule-013: run scripts/live-check.mjs unattended as a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow against https://repoglance.com (daily, plus workflow_dispatch), building main and failing loudly on any <main> difference or a non-seed, non-synced source; no secrets, no Cloudflare change, the pages are public. It closes the gap this cycle leaves between maintainer runs: drift is caught within a day instead of at the next deploy.
